text:
carlos.prod: Hey team — several customers reporting Console hourly usage stopped updating ~6h after we did the ETL redeploy at 01:12 UTC. Dashboard shows last datapoint at 19:00 local. Any idea?

maya.support: thanks for flagging, carlos. can you paste a tenant id or org id affected?

carlos.prod: acme-inc (org_792). I can repro in the console: hourly heatmap blank for last 6 intervals.

deploy-bot: deploy finished "etl-worker-v2" commit abc123 at 2024-11-08T01:12:07Z (outcome: success) :rocket:

jonathan.data: looking. main suspects: consumer group offset reset or job ordering where aggregator started before connector warmed. checking kafka lag now.

priya.sre: there was a rolling restart of etl-worker nodes at 01:10-01:18 — healthchecks passed but we saw a short spike in commit errors in logs.

jonathan.data: from the consumer group check:
```
$ kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-main:9092 --group hourly-agg-group --describe
TOPIC           PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG  CONSUMER-ID
usage_raw       0          1245223         1245223         0    -
usage_raw       1          1241800         1249932         8132 consumer-1
usage_raw       2          1240999         1249999         9000 consumer-2
```

jonathan.data: partitions 1/2 show ~8–9k lag. looks like two consumers never committed after redeploy.

maya.support: is that consistent with the tenants showing gaps? acme-inc maps to partition 1.

carlos.prod: yes acme is on partition 1.

priya.sre: grabbing recent etl logs for consumer-1: saw repeated error "Failed to commit offsets: OffsetCommitRequest failed" around 01:13. stack trace shows connection reset to broker; then consumer process restarted and rejoined but used earliest reset policy, so committed offset moved back.

jonathan.data: probable root cause: race during redeploy — aggregator started before connector had fully reprocessed in-memory state causing missed commits and downstream aggregator waiting for watermark. That caused hourly-rollup job to skip windows until Kafka lag cleared.

lina.product: customers seeing "no data" on console — is this safe to backfill? do we risk double-counting?

jonathan.data: backfill is safe if we use the idempotent job path (uses upserts into rollup table keyed by tenant+hour). I'll run a targeted reprocess for affected partitions/offset ranges.

maya.support: ETA? I need reply for customer comms.

jonathan.data: starting targeted reprocess for topic usage_raw partition 1 from offset 1241800 to 1249932 now. command:
```
$ airflow trigger_dag hourly_agg_backfill --conf '{"topic":"usage_raw","partition":1,"start_offset":1241800,"end_offset":1249932}'
```

deploy-bot: DAG hourly_agg_backfill run 2024-11-08T02:05Z enqueued.

jonathan.data: progress: about 30% through, currently processing offsets ~1244000. estimated 20m.

carlos.prod: noted, sharing with acme support lead.

priya.sre: monitoring consumer lags and the aggregator service. also adding a guard to prevent aggregator start before connectors report healthy.

jonathan.data: backfill finished. checksums match expected, upsert counts: 8.1k rows applied for partition 1.

maya.support: can confirm acme-inc dashboard updated and shows the missing hours. i'm posting a short note to the customer. :white_check_mark:

lina.product: filing a postmortem action: add deploy ordering check + alert when consumer lag > 1k after deploy.

jonathan.data: created ticket INF-4827 with run details and SQL used for verification. attaching offsets and md5s.

carlos.prod: thanks everyone. can we add an FAQ blurb for customers if they see temporary gaps post-maintenance?

maya.support: good idea — will draft and share.

priya.sre: followups: (1) add startup dependency, (2) alert on >15m sustained lag for hourly-agg-group, (3) add automated backfill job that triggers when lag crosses threshold. i'll own 1+2.

jonathan.data: I'll schedule the auto-backfill prototype and link to ticket.

maya.support: leaving this thread open until docs/alerts are in place. closing notes to customer: we identified a race during ETL redeploy that caused consumer commits to fail briefly; targeted backfill applied successfully and dashboards restored.
